goal: Use the Reasoning Learning Suite to evaluate a real reasoning route performed by ChatGPT against the suite itself, identify measurement holes, and define the next optimization experiment.
starting_state: Suite bootstrap workflow had passed, but only one bootstrap procedure record existed and actor latency/verification metrics were null.

route.action: Recover exact prior suite state before acting
route.input_shape: focused continuation query naming suite, branch, workflow, analyzer, schema, bootstrap and testing principles

route.action: Discover only workflow-related GitHub operations needed for live inspection
route.input_shape: GitHub path filtered by single keyword workflow

route.action: Inspect actual bootstrap execution rather than trusting green workflow status
route.input_shape: known repository plus known successful job id

route.action: Discover file operation required to inspect schema before writing a new run
route.input_shape: GitHub path filtered by single keyword file

route.action: Read current ProcedureRun schema at the exact staging branch
route.input_shape: known repository, exact schema path, exact branch

route.action: Persist this self-test as a second empirical procedure run
route.input_shape: schema-conforming JSON record on isolated staging branch

friction: The suite currently depends on manually authored procedure records; it cannot automatically observe ChatGPT connector calls.
Tool latency values visible in connector responses are not automatically captured into ProcedureRun records.
The workflow summary aggregates actor latency only when records contain actual_latency_ms, so the first summary reported null latency for all actors.
ambiguities: Verification cost is currently an uncalibrated numeric field; values are comparable only weakly until a scale is defined.
Procedure efficiency cannot yet be inferred from one route because there is no competing route for the same task class.
holes: No automatic trace ingestion from connector/tool execution into run records.
No normalized quality score combining correctness, evidence, latency, calls, verification burden and recovery cost.
No promotion threshold preventing a one-off routing observation from becoming a default rule.
repairs: Record the recursive self-test as a second empirical run rather than describing it only in conversation.
Use exact branch/path reads before writes to keep the suite self-consistent.
Treat missing latency as missing evidence, not zero latency.
Require repeated or paired-route evidence before ADOPT_DEFAULT.

evidence: Job 99295585565 ran 3 analyzer tests successfully in 0.002s.
Bootstrap summary had run_count=1, product_outcome BLOCKED=1, procedure_outcome ACCEPTABLE=1.
Bootstrap summary reported null mean and median latency for all three recorded GitHub actors.
Current ProcedureRun schema explicitly supports actual_latency_ms, expected_latency_ms, verification_cost, synchronization classes, reusable/negative rules and next experiments.
reusable_rule: A reasoning-learning system must evaluate its own observation route as data; green CI proves machinery health but optimization claims require measured competing routes and non-null performance evidence.
negative_rule: Do not call a reasoning route faster, smarter, or default-worthy when latency, verification burden, and a comparison baseline have not actually been measured.
next_experiment: Run two materially different GitHub retrieval routes against the same repository question, capture connector latency from each call, count calls and verification operations, verify both answers against the same source evidence, then compare effective route cost before adopting either route.
